transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sarah Gomez (AmberTech - Head of AI), Raj Malik (AmberTech - Infra), Nina Park (AmberTech - Product), Eli Torres (AmberTech - SRE)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics. Demo covered streaming responses, key generation parameters, retry patterns and best practices, plus a short tour of Redwood Console and Optimize suggestions. Customer asked about data retention, SOC 2, VPC options, and latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps to run a short bench and exchange sample prompts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this, we've got Liam from our SE team, quick intro from ambertech?
[00:06] Sarah Gomez: Hi yeah Sarah here, head of AI at AmberTech, excited to see your hosted API, we're evaluating for chat generation in our support product.
[00:11] Raj Malik: Raj infra, i'll be helping with the bench and network questions.
[00:14] Nina Park: Nina product, i'll be owning success criteria.
[00:17] Liam Chen: Nice to meet you all, i'll walk through the demo and the streaming samples. Quick agenda: show hosted API chat + text gen, streaming, params, retries/backoff, then Console and a few Optimize tips.
[00:28] Sarah Gomez: sounds good, our main constraints are latency under 200ms 95p for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens target, also SSO and SOC2 checklist.
[00:38] Maya Patel: perfect, that's helpful. quick q, are you leaning hosted vs dedicated/private?
[00:42] Sarah Gomez: initial preference is hosted for speed, but we may need a dedicated pool for PII workloads later.
[00:47] Liam Chen: Great, i'll keep that in mind when we talk about routing and model variants. Ok demo -> i'll share my screen.
[01:02] [screen share noises]
[01:15] Liam Chen: so here's a simple POST to /v1/chat/completions, payload with messages, you can stream with chunked-encoding, we stream token deltas as they are generated. Example code in node/python shows using a streaming ws or server-sent events.
[01:34] Sarah Gomez: that streaming piece is important, we want the UI to show partial responses as they arrive, do you need special client code?
[01:39] Liam Chen: just a standard streaming consumer. here's an example with SSE and another with websockets. small caveat: if you want to resume after a network blip, we recommend using chunk ids + client-side concat, we don't support full resume of KV cache over new session in hosted mode yet.
[01:58] Raj Malik: when you say KV cache not resumable, does that mean repeated prefixes incur full cost?
[02:03] Liam Chen: correct for hosted default; we do prefix caching on the server for repeated requests from same route but full KV checkpoint restore is a dedicated/private feature. that's one of the tradeoffs we discussed.
[02:16] Nina Park: how about retries? we have transient 503s from other vendors sometimes.
[02:20] Liam Chen: recommended pattern: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 attempts, idempotency keys on request metadata when possible. we also surface 429 vs 503 so you can differentiate throttling vs infra errors.
[02:33] Sarah Gomez: any example retry headers or sdk defaults?
[02:36] Liam Chen: our SDKs default to a single retry for transient network errors, but we ship a retry helper in the js/python snippets — i'll share that. also show circuit breaker example if you're doing high QPS.
[02:48] Maya Patel: i'll attach the retry snippet and recommended backoff parameters in the follow-up.
[02:52] [brief cross-talk]
[03:03] Liam Chen: next, params — temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalty. for chat we send system/user/assistant roles. low temperature for deterministic replies, higher for creativity. also show sampling seeds rarely used.
[03:22] Raj Malik: what about tokenization? does cost map to tokens we send or tokens generated?
[03:26] Liam Chen: both; cost is per-token for input + output. Console exposes token breakdown per request at a route level so you can see which prompts are expensive.
[03:35] Sarah Gomez: great. can you show the Console?
[03:38] Liam Chen: switching to Console view — ok per-route dashboard, latency percentiles, token-level cost, burst metrics. you can pin SLOs and setup alerts on regression. here's an example trace for a slow request and the token breakdown.
[04:05] Nina Park: is it possible to see per-user or per-api-key usage? we need cost allocation by team.
[04:10] Liam Chen: yes, by token-level tagging and per-key dashboards, you can slice by api key, region, model. retention windows are configurable depending on plan.
[04:18] Sarah Gomez: retention configurable — what's default and do you support stricter retention for compliance?
[04:23] Maya Patel: hosted defaults to 30 days for logs and traces, but enterprise plans can get custom retention or private deployments with customer-managed retention. we'll share SOC2 and data flow docs.
[04:32] Raj Malik: SSO and RBAC? we need SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[04:36] Maya Patel: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles for team members, and audit logs. for encryption we support KMS integrations for private deployments, hosted uses provider-managed keys but enterprise options available.
[04:51] Sarah Gomez: great. any mention of SOC2?
[04:53] Maya Patel: we are SOC2 Type II. i'll attach the report under NDA.
[04:58] Sarah Gomez: ok thanks.
[05:02] Liam Chen: back to streaming for UX: we also recommend short max_tokens for incremental responses, you can stream as you go and if you need to continue context, we append assistant deltas to the conversation. note on retries: with streaming it's trickier — we recommend client-side buffering and idempotency for finalization calls.
[05:28] Nina Park: curious about batching and costs — you mentioned Optimize earlier?
[05:32] Liam Chen: yes Redwood Optimize suggests batching and caching strategies. example: if you have many similar prompts, prefix caching can save tokens. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles if you run ded- or private, but for hosted we can suggest parameter settings and recommended model variants to hit latency vs cost targets.
[05:50] Sarah Gomez: any quick numbers for latency on your catalog models?
[05:53] Liam Chen: depends on sequence length; for short prompts we see 50–120ms p95 on our curated small models; larger models will be higher. we'll provide a model performance spreadsheet.
[06:05] Raj Malik: network egress and region — do you have multi-region endpoints?
[06:09] Liam Chen: yes regional endpoints, and smart routing to fallback regions; we can pin requests to region for data residency.
[06:16] Eli Torres: regarding throughput, if we ramp to 200 QPS, how do you handle rate limits?
[06:21] Maya Patel: we support quota config and bursting for hosted customers, and for committed capacity customers we recommend Dedicated. SLA for latency/uptime available on Dedicated/Enterprise tiers.
[06:34] Sarah Gomez: can you run a short bench with our infra? we'd like to measure end-to-end latency from our client to your hosted endpoint under typical network conditions.
[06:41] Maya Patel: yes we can, we'll need your network poke points and preferred times. Raj if you can share topology that helps.
[06:48] Raj Malik: will do, i'll send a diagram and preferred windows.
[06:52] Liam Chen: one more thing — observability hooks: tracing header X-Redwood-Trace and you can ingest traces into your system or use our console. for retry and backoff, we include reason codes in headers to help debugging.
[07:06] Sarah Gomez: ok nice. now to do a quick live prompt sample?
[07:10] Liam Chen: yes — i'll run a sample conversation. sending prompt: "support: customer says their order didn't arrive, summarize and propose next steps."
[07:22] [streaming tokens appear]
[07:25] Liam Chen: you'll see deltas come in, UI updates as tokens arrive — partial sentence then completes.
[07:35] Sarah Gomez: looks clean, any hallucination mitigation? we use retrieval augmented generation for product data.
[07:40] Liam Chen: retrieval: you can call embeddings + rerank or pass context in system messages. we recommend chunking docs and use a similarity-retrieval pipeline. we also provide confidence scoring hooks and rule-based filters at the app layer.
[07:56] Nina Park: is there guardrails support like function calling?
[07:59] Liam Chen: yes we support structured outputs and function/tool calling patterns — you can define function schemas and the model will return JSON-ish structures, though sometimes the transcription of those fields can be imperfect so validate on the client.
[08:12] Sarah Gomez: ok good.
[08:14] Liam Chen: circling back to errors and status codes: 4xx for bad request, 429 for rate limits, 5xx for infra — we return a retry-after header on 429. for streaming partial errors we include a final status chunk.
[08:29] Raj Malik: curious about cost control — can we cap tokens per user or per key?
[08:33] Maya Patel: yes per-key quotas and per-route limits, and cost alerts in Console. you can also pre-process prompts to reduce token count, e.g., shorter system messages.
[08:45] Sarah Gomez: anything else about security before we close?
[08:48] Maya Patel: i'll send SOC2 and data-flow diagram; for sensitive workloads we recommend Private with customer-managed keys, or Dedicated with strict egress rules. you can also enforce data residency.
[09:03] Nina Park: timeline question: if we decide to pilot, how fast can we start?
[09:07] Maya Patel: hosted trial can be provisioned in 24–48 hours; bench runs scheduled within a week depending on schedules; Dedicated/Private takes longer (multi-week) due to infra setup.
[09:18] Sarah Gomez: budget owner will need pricing, and product will need success criteria. we'll share prompts and expected QPS.
[09:25] Maya Patel: noted. i'll follow up with pricing and the trial link.
[09:29] Liam Chen: i'll drop the streaming notebook and retry helpers in the thread.
[09:33] [wrap-up]
[09:36] Maya Patel: recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing/trial, Liam sends code samples, AmberTech to share prompts and bench windows. Action items in calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
[09:47] Sarah Gomez: thanks all, this was helpful.
[09:50] Raj Malik: thanks.
[09:52] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: moderate; occasional words may be mis-attributed and some technical terms like "KV cache" may appear as "K-V cash". References shared during the call: link to hosted API docs (https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted-api), streaming demo repo (link provided by Liam), pricing sheet (to be shared), SOC2 report (will be shared under NDA).
